video.title: Fantasy Basketball Small Forward Tier Rankings [NBA]

summary: Josh Lloyd ranks small forwards for fantasy drafts in eight tiers, using Fantrax positional eligibility. Jayson Tatum is alone in tier one and is fine in round one. Kevin Durant and Cooper Flagg make up tier two, and Scottie Barnes, Jalen Johnson and Austin Reaves make up tier three. He thinks Barnes, Johnson, Deni Avdija, Lauri Markkanen and Desmond Bane will come back down because of new teammates. He likes Paul George, Matas Buzelis, Jalen Williams, Brandon Ingram and Gui Santos at their prices. He thinks Kon Knueppel, Mikal Bridges, AJ Dybantsa, Aaron Nesmith and Kawhi Leonard (at his ADP) are being drafted too early. He also argues that tiers have limited use in category leagues because players in the same tier help in very different categories.

rules.text: Tiers have limited use in category leagues and even points leagues. Players in the same tier can give completely different category profiles, so draft for the categories you need.
rules.quote: the utility of tier tiers for category leagues, even points leagues, is not really that high

rules.text: A player being healthy last season does not mean he will be healthy this season.
rules.quote: because he was healthy last season, he will be healthy this season. That would be antithetical

rules.text: Availability is not the best ability. Many low-value players played 82 games, so games played alone should not push a player up the draft board.
rules.quote: availability is the best ability. It's actually not. The best ability is ability.

rules.text: When a team adds high-usage players (for example several new guards or scorers), the existing star's usage and assist upside drops, even if his minutes stay the same.
rules.quote: the usage and passing upside for Denny I think is dropped down and those guys will miss time

rules.text: Even if new teammates miss games, they still play more than zero games, so the player still loses some production compared to last season.
rules.quote: unless they're playing zero games that means they're doing more than last season

rules.text: Look at the context behind a breakout season, such as which teammates were out. Big numbers posted while key teammates were missing should be scaled back.
rules.quote: Bane did a lot of his damage on insane shooting stuff when Vagnner was out

rules.text: Late-season numbers on tanking teams can be fake because everyone is out and no one is trying.
rules.quote: his numbers down the stretch were fake because everyone was out and no one was trying

rules.text: Late-draft hedge strategy: draft both candidates in a starting-job battle, see which one wins it, and cut the other.
rules.quote: you take him and Yakul Linderborg. You see which one wins the starting job and you cut

rules.text: In deeper leagues such as 14 teams, late-round players become close to starters and are worth more.
rules.quote: if we're heading more into like 14 team leagues where players in this range become close enough

rules.text: Players with injury risk get pushed down a tier or more. He will not draft Kawhi Leonard before pick 40 or in round two.
rules.quote: Kawhai would be like a tier 2 player if I didn't have any worries about his injuries

rules.text: Some players are worth very different amounts in points leagues and category leagues, so rank them separately for each format.
rules.quote: There is a big difference between Durant in category leagues and points leagues.

rules.text: When public perception of an injured player drops a lot but your valuation stays the same, you can get value by drafting him.
rules.quote: public perception has changed a lot where I'd be very happy to be drafting uh Jaylen Williams
